title: Find the Number of Distinct Colors Among the Balls
summary: Given an integer limit and a 2D array queries, mark each ball x with color y for every query [x, y].
statement: Given an integer limit and a 2D array queries, mark each ball x with color y for every query [x, y]. After each query, determine the count of distinct colors among the balls. Return an array where each element represents the number of distinct colors after the corresponding query.
constraints: Ball labels range from zero through limit; queries is nonempty and every color is positive.
Each query [ball,color] replaces that ball’s previous color, if any.
After every update, return the number of different colors currently assigned to at least one ball.
hints: Track both directions needed by updates: each ball’s current color and each color’s number of balls.
On replacement decrement and possibly delete the old color, then increment the new color.
Update ball_color and color_count; append len(color_count).
A color is present exactly when its maintained frequency is positive, so the map size is the desired distinct count.
editorial: A color is present exactly when its maintained frequency is positive, so the map size is the desired distinct count.

tests.explanation: The distinct-color counts after replacement are one, two, two, and three.
The two balls first share color one; recoloring ball zero produces two distinct colors.
